indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.4.3.2: Recognise some simple machines and their advantages of making work easier
indicator.objective: Identify simple machines used for specific work

skills.description: Identify simple machines used for specific work
Match a simple machine to the specific task it performs
Demonstrate or describe how to use a simple machine safely to complete a specific task
Explain why a specific simple machine is the right tool for a specific job

misconceptions: Any tool can do any job.
A screwdriver can be used as a hammer.
Simple machines do the work for you without you doing anything.
Scissors are only for cutting paper; they cannot cut cloth.
Only complex machines (like cars or computers) are machines.

questions.stem: Which of these is a simple machine used for cutting paper?
questions.explanation: Scissors are a simple machine used for cutting paper, cloth, and other materials.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a spoon can cut paper.

questions.stem: Which simple machine is used to open a bottle of soft drink?
hints: You use it in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: A bottle opener is a simple machine specifically designed to remove bottle caps.
questions.misconception: Pupils may try to use a spoon or their teeth.

questions.stem: Which simple machine is used to sweep the floor?
questions.explanation: A broom is a simple machine used for sweeping.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider a broom a machine.

questions.stem: Ama wants to remove a nail from a piece of wood. Which tool should she use?
questions.explanation: A claw hammer is used for removing nails.
questions.misconception: Pupils may try to use scissors.

questions.stem: Which simple machine is used for cutting cloth?
questions.explanation: Scissors are used for cutting cloth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think scissors are only for paper.

questions.stem: Kofi is using a bottle opener. How should he hold it to open the bottle safely?
options: Point the sharp edge at his face
Hold it firmly and place it on the cap, then lift
hints: You need to grip the cap.
Do not point it at yourself.
questions.explanation: You should hold the opener firmly, place it correctly on the cap, and lift to remove the cap safely.
questions.misconception: Pupils may use tools incorrectly if not shown.

questions.stem: Why is a wheelbarrow useful for carrying heavy loads?
options: It has a wheel that helps it roll, making it easier to move heavy things
questions.explanation: A wheelbarrow has a wheel that reduces friction, making it easier to move heavy loads with less effort.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the wheelbarrow magically reduces the weight.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a simple machine?
hints: Which one is an electronic device?
It has a screen and needs electricity.
questions.explanation: A television is an electronic device, not a simple machine.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all tools are simple machines.

questions.stem: Which simple machine would you use to tighten a screw into a piece of wood?
hints: It has a shaped tip for screws.
questions.explanation: A screwdriver is used to turn and tighten screws.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a hammer is for screws.

questions.stem: Ama is using scissors to cut a piece of cloth. What is the safest way to hold the scissors?
hints: You put your fingers through loops.
questions.explanation: You should hold scissors by the handles to keep your fingers away from the sharp blades.
questions.misconception: Pupils may hold the blades, which is dangerous.

questions.stem: Why do we use a spoon rather than a fork to eat fufu?
options: A spoon can scoop and hold the soft fufu better than a fork
hints: A spoon has a bowl shape.
questions.explanation: A spoon is the right tool for eating fufu because its shape can scoop and hold the soft food, while a fork would just pierce it and let it fall.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any tool can eat any food.

questions.stem: Name the simple machine you would use to cut paper.
questions.explanation: Scissors are used to cut paper.

questions.stem: Name one simple machine you can find in a kitchen.
hints: You use it to open bottles.
You use it to cut or peel food.
questions.explanation: A bottle opener or a knife are simple machines found in the kitchen.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name an electronic device like a microwave.

questions.stem: Ama wants to open a tin of tomatoes. She only has a spoon, a hammer, a bottle opener, and a tin cutter. Which is the right tool and why?
options: A tin cutter, because it is made to cut metal tins safely
A hammer, because it can smash the tin
A spoon, because it is small
A bottle opener, because it is metal
hints: Which tool is designed for tins?
Using a hammer would be dangerous and messy.
questions.explanation: A tin cutter is the correct simple machine designed to safely open metal tins.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose dangerous improvised tools.

questions.stem: Why does a broom make sweeping easier than using your bare hands?
options: The broom handle reaches further and the bristles gather dirt better
hints: Think about the length of the handle.
questions.explanation: A broom makes sweeping easier because the long handle lets you reach the floor without bending, and the bristles gather dirt efficiently.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not think about the physical advantage of the tool.

questions.stem: Kofi is trying to pull a nail out of a piece of wood using a hammer. He holds the hammer by the head and tries to pull. Why is this wrong?
options: He should hold the handle to get leverage and use the claw part
He should use the flat part
hints: You need to grip the handle.
questions.explanation: Kofi should hold the hammer by the handle to get a good grip and leverage, and use the claw part to grip and pull the nail.
questions.misconception: Pupils may use tools incorrectly without understanding leverage.

questions.stem: Which simple machine would a tailor use to remove a stubborn button from a shirt?
hints: They need to cut the thread.
questions.explanation: A tailor would use scissors to cut the thread holding the button.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose a tool that would damage the shirt.

questions.stem: Explain why it is better to use a wheelbarrow to carry stones than to carry them in your hands.

criteria.description: States that the wheelbarrow holds more stones
States that the wheel helps roll the load, reducing the effort needed

hints: How many stones can you carry in your hands?
questions.explanation: A wheelbarrow carries more stones and the wheel reduces the effort needed to move the heavy load.

questions.stem: Show your teacher how to safely use a pair of scissors to cut a straight line on a piece of paper.

criteria.description: Keeps fingers away from the blades

hints: Put your fingers in the loops.
questions.explanation: This tests the safe and correct use of a simple machine.

questions.stem: Ama says 'I can use a spoon to cut my meat.' Why is this a bad idea?
options: A spoon is not sharp and cannot cut meat; a knife is the right tool
A spoon is made of metal
A spoon is for soup only
hints: Spoons are for scooping, not cutting.
questions.explanation: A spoon is not designed to cut. It would squash the meat instead of cutting it. A knife is the correct simple machine for cutting meat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may try to use the wrong tool for a job.
